title: Crypto qualifications need clear process
full_text:
SMSF auditors questioning whether to raise issues about cryptocurrency held within a fund must be clear Part A and Part B qualification are separate decisions, while recognising one may lead to the other, an industry professional has highlighted.
Tactical Super director Jacob Kewley said while Part A related to the financial report for the fund and Part B was about its compliance with the superannuation law and regulations, cryptocurrency and digital asset holdings often touch on both areas and needed to be addressed accordingly.
“Part A is where we address the existence of the assets, the rights to ownership and their valuation,” Kewley said at the recent Auditors Institute Auditors Day 2026 in Melbourne.
“Part B needs a provision to be breached, such as [Superannuation Industry (Supervision) (SIS) Regulation 4.09a] separation of assets, [Regulation 8.02b] assets valued at market value, and [SIS Act section 66] acquisition from a related party, which are going to be most likely affected for the audit report.”
He used the example of a significant balance held on a crypto-exchange, but lacking a controlled audit report from that platform, as a way to proceed with qualifying a fund’s audit report.
“The lack of an audit report is indicative, but by itself it doesn’t affect the opinion. If you’ve got the exchange statements, the back trail, the full history and independent pricing, you could conclude an unmodified opinion [from the platform] is consistent,” he added.
“I don’t think so. The lack of a type two controlled audit report lands heavily into at least a part A qualification, and that’s your decision as auditor with your reporting obligations and how you write your audit report.
“You then have to determine if that leads you to a Part B qualification. I think that’s defensible, but also not automatic and that’s tough. Probably the safest position would be to breach both and do an audit contravention report.
“Whatever you do, your position has to be documented in the file and it has to be complete.”
author: Jason Spits
